title: Choose Jade Learning's visual world
question: The roll assigned Letter Tiles on the Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Letter Tiles on the Board
options.lineage: wooden letter-tile board games on the kitchen table
options.thesis: Every letter is a physical tile the speller places, so a spelling becomes an object you can check piece by piece.
materials: maple letter tiles with a pressed-ink letter and soft bevel
coloured premium squares as the only colour fields
options.viewport: Laptop or iPad: jade board fills the screen; a big round Say-it button and a rack of bee questions (Definition, Sentence, Origin) sit above a row of empty tile squares; typing drops maple tiles into the squares; Check is a marigold key-tile.
options.risk: Tiles must stay a spelling tool, not a board-game costume; if the board decorates instead of grading, it reads as a theme.

raised.raise: The correct spelling reveals tile by tile in a cascade, one letter per beat, synced to the voice spelling it aloud.
Feedback colour lives on tile edges and underlines only; the letter ink stays dark on every tile so words stay readable.
Each colour is one law everywhere: marigold means right, coral means wrong letter, sky means missing, stone means extra. No colour means anything else.
Mastery is a fixed five-step ramp of pips on every word tile (the Leitner box), identical on the play screen, results, and the parent view.
Every feedback line points at the exact tile it is about (“ie, not ei” under those two tiles); no generic “Oops”.

options.label: Spelling Bee Stage
options.lineage: the school auditorium bee: curtain, mic stand, contestant placard
options.thesis: Each round is a turn at the microphone: the speller steps into the spotlight, asks the pronouncer, and spells.
options.viewport: Dark stage with a spotlight on the word slot, the speller's placard bottom-left, pronouncer questions as cue cards.
options.risk: The most literal reading of the brief and a common landing spot; dark stage can feel high-pressure for a nervous speller.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Each word is a row of flap cells that clack into place, letter by letter.
options.viewport: A single departure-board row as the answer field; the list below as upcoming 'departures'.
options.case: Holds product clarity (fixed character cells, cascading reveal) but 8–11 spellers rarely know the object.
options.risk: Condensed caps flatten letter shapes kids learn in lowercase; can feel cold.

options.label: Arcade Pixel Glow
options.lineage: pixel-art arcade cabinets and handheld games
options.thesis: Spelling as a level: every word a room, every letter a sprite.
options.viewport: Pixel HUD with score top edge; the word slot is a tile row in the playfield.
options.case: Holds audience identification (kids live in games) but pixel type hurts exactly the letterforms being learned.
options.risk: Legibility of letters, the core content, degrades.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.thesis: Quiet white field with spectral colour only at the edges.
options.viewport: Achromatic page, feedback as thin coloured fringes.
options.case: Loses both axes: kids don't identify, and pastel fringes weaken feedback.
options.kept: Colour confined to edges so text stays achromatic and legible.

options.label: Gravity-rain Garden
options.thesis: Colour-coded rain obeys its cloud's gravity.
options.viewport: A garden where letters fall to their slots.
options.case: Loses both: whimsy obscures a spelling task.
options.kept: One colour, one law, applied without exception.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.viewport: Words as stars sized by mastery.
options.case: Loses both: abstract for the task.
options.kept: A fixed ramp that always encodes the same thing.

options.label: Monochrome Product Canon
options.thesis: Every claim paired with the detail that proves it.
options.kept: Every statement paired with its proof.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A bright, friendly learning app: white cards, rounded buttons, a cheerful primary colour and a mascot.
canonCard.viewport: Centered card with the word prompt, big green Check button, progress bar on top.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every kids' learning app by design.
